text: Ivan Rebroff (born Hans Rolf Rippert; 31 July 1931 – 27 February 2008) was a German vocalist allegedly of Russian ancestry, known for his distinctive and extensive vocal range of four octaves, spanning from a low F to a high F, one and a quarter octaves above C. An imposing figure on stage, he was typically bearded and dressed in Cossack clothing, with his height exceeding 2 metres. Born on 31 July 1931 in Berlin, he claimed to have been born prematurely at seven months on a train platform, a statement he made in his own account. His parents were Paul Rippert, an engineer born in 1897 in Liebenwerda, and Luise Fenske, born in Bromberg (now Bydgoszcz, Poland). While his Russian descent is often disputed, it has never been entirely refuted; in a 1989 interview with Izvestia, he stated "according to documents I am Ivan Pavlovich Rebroff" (Russian: Иван Павлович Ребров). He studied singing at the Hochschule für Musik und Theater Hamburg. Despite imperfect knowledge and pronunciation of Russian, he gained fame for performing Russian folk songs, as well as opera, light classics, and folk songs from various other countries. Known for his stage enthusiasm, he performed over 6,000 concerts, including a two-year, seven-day-a-week engagement at the Théâtre Marigny in Paris, where he portrayed Tevye in Fiddler on the Roof. In his seventies, he still performed 13 concerts in 21 days during an Australian tour. Rebroff described himself as the "connection between East and West." He was named an honorary citizen of the Greek Sporades island of Skopelos, his domicile. Rebroff was privately homosexual. In addition to singing, he was at least a reasonable violinist and keyboardist, as evidenced by photographs of him playing a church organ, though he may have also played the piano. He sang and could converse to varying degrees in Russian, French, Italian, English, and Greek, in addition to his native German. He died at the age of 76 in Frankfurt on 27 February 2008, following a long illness. Four days after his death, his brother Horst Rippert [de], who is nine years his senior and, according to his own unsubstantiated claims, shot down Antoine de Saint-Exupéry during World War II, claimed part of Rebroff's vast fortune.
